verdict.rationale: Open WebUI documents a cross-conversation memory system, and users can manually add, edit, or delete memories under Settings > Personalization > Memory. Because the platform is self-hosted and built to run entirely offline, the memory store plausibly stays on the user's own machine, but no evidence describes the storage format. Missing for 10: documentation that memories are stored in an open, user-readable format; explicit statement of where the memory store lives on disk; independent or hands-on corroboration of the inspect/edit/delete workflow.

support.subject: As a privacy-first user, I can inspect, edit, and delete what the assistant has remembered — the memory store lives on my machine in an open format

citations.quote: Users can manually add, edit, or delete memories by navigating to: Settings > Personalization > Memory
Open WebUI includes a sophisticated memory system that allows models to remember facts, preferences, and context across different conversations.
self-hosted AI platform that's extensible, feature-rich, user-friendly, and built to run entirely offline
